title: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight
hook: a teacher walks onto the field just as his two best students raise their maces at each other

segments.voice: Your line was Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight. Yesterday Yudhishthira made a risky offer, and the hidden king came up out of the water to take it. Did you count the risk before an offer? Day eight hundred forty-seven.

Two men face each other on open ground, each holding a heavy iron mace. One is Bhima, of the Pandava brothers. The other is Duryodhana, the Kaurava king, wet from the lake he hid in. And just then a third man arrives, fresh from a long pilgrimage along the holy river Sarasvati. It's Balarama, Krishna's elder brother. He taught both of these men how to fight with the mace. He has stayed out of the whole war. Now he has come back in time to watch his two students try to kill each other. Today, how the mace fight goes, and the signal that ends it.
screen: `TWO MEN, TWO MACES.` → `A TEACHER ARRIVES.` → `BOTH ARE HIS STUDENTS.`

segments.voice: Balarama greets everyone, and he asks for the fight to move. In Ganguli's telling, they all walk to Samantapanchaka, ground held holy, so that a warrior who dies there dies in a sacred place. Then the two cousins close in. The epic gives the fight like weather: maces crashing, sparks flying, the two circling each other like bulls. Neither gives way. On the edge of the ground, Arjuna turns to Krishna and asks, in effect, which of them is better. Krishna's answer is careful. Bhima is the stronger, he says. Duryodhana has put in more practice and has more skill. Fought by the rules, Bhima may not win. And then Krishna reminds Arjuna of something said years before, in the dice hall. When Draupadi was dragged in and insulted, Duryodhana bared his thigh to her, and Bhima vowed to break that thigh with his mace. Arjuna understands. Standing where Bhima can see him, he strikes his own thigh with his hand. Bhima sees it. When Duryodhana next leaps into the air, Bhima swings low, a blow that the rules of mace fighting forbid, and breaks both his thighs. The king falls. So this week ran from Karna's stuck wheel, through Shalya's command, to this one blow on a holy plain. And the man who just arrived, the teacher of both fighters, has seen all of it.
screen: `MOVE TO HOLY GROUND` · `STRONGER VERSUS SKILLED` · `ARJUNA STRIKES HIS OWN THIGH` · then, large: `THE BLOW BELOW THE WAIST`

segments.voice: Sit with both feet flat on the floor and rest your hands on your thighs. Feel their weight, and the strength in your legs that carries you all day without being asked. Breathe in, and notice that strength. Breathe out, and let the legs go soft. Then bring to mind a time someone signaled you without a word, a look or a gesture you understood at once. Don't judge what followed. Just hold that moment for a few breaths and see it clearly. If you pray, you can hold it in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Shalya. The book of the war's last day: a king out of the lake, a teacher arriving, and a vow kept with one blow below the waist.

Your line: Shalya: Duryodhana in the lake, the mace fight. Today, catch one signal you give without a word, a look, a sigh, a shrug, and ask what it tells the person who reads it. Tomorrow, the teacher's anger. Day eight hundred forty-seven.

howItsDone: The mace fight between Bhima and Duryodhana is a favorite scene in retellings, dance-dramas and recitations of the Mahabharata, and Bhima is often shown in art holding his mace.

myth: Balarama fought on the Pandava side through the war
he stayed away on pilgrimage and arrived only for the mace fight.
Krishna said Bhima might not win by the rules
he called Bhima the stronger and Duryodhana the more skilled.
Bhima's blow to the thigh was within the rules of mace fighting
the blow below the waist was forbidden, and he struck it to keep a vow from the dice hall.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. Krishna has just told you Bhima may lose if he fights by the rules, and reminded you of Bhima's vow. what do you do?
options: strike your own thigh where Bhima can see.
step in and fight Duryodhana yourself.
fork.reveal: Arjuna strikes his own thigh, Bhima reads the sign, and his next blow breaks Duryodhana's thighs.

original.note: mace: the heavy club Bhima and Duryodhana both learned from Balarama.

trapdoor: what you thought: Bhima won a fair fight because he was stronger.
what it means: Krishna said Bhima might lose by the rules, and the winning blow broke them.
what a scholar hears: the blow lands on the thigh Duryodhana bared to Draupadi, so a vow from the dice hall closes the war's last duel.
